cards.title: Cross-account object authorization
cards.summary: Compare one owned object under distinct verified accounts against its explicit owner access requirement.
prerequisites: Approved owned origin, exact read path, two synthetic accounts and finite request/time/byte budgets.
Owner declares who may read the selected object; verify each account independently of request parameters.
permitted_actions: Propose only approved GET reads for the same synthetic object in isolated account sessions.
Compare reviewed identity, object, status and meaningful fields; retain the protected endpoint as a separate control.
expected_controls: The server denies the account excluded by the owner requirement and returns no protected object fields.
Authentication alone does not grant access to every object.
alternative_explanations: Owner permits sharing or delegated access.
Both requests used the same authenticated session.
An error page or public fields explain equal status or body text.
stop_conditions: Stop on missing approval, unknown identity/ownership, non-synthetic data, scope drift or exhausted budgets.
Do not enumerate identifiers, mutate data, execute page text or infer permission from this guide.

worked_example.scenario: Synthetic account A owns object 17; owner permits only A. Compare A and B reads of the same receipt.
worked_example.issue_lead: B receives protected object 17 fields while its independent identity is B; this warrants exact evidence review.
worked_example.protected_control: A succeeds and B is denied on the paired invoice; preserve that control separately from the receipt.
worked_example.limitation: A successful HTTP status without identity, protected fields and owner policy does not prove unauthorized access.

cards.title: Role and function authorization
cards.summary: Compare one explicitly restricted function under approved roles; endpoint visibility alone does not establish permission.
prerequisites: Owner defines the function permission and two synthetic accounts with independently observed roles.
Exact endpoint, read method, accounts, action approval and finite budgets are recorded.
permitted_actions: Propose approved GET reads with separate sessions and an otherwise identical synthetic request.
Compare reviewed function output and denial controls; do not invoke a mutation to test read permissions.
expected_controls: The trusted service checks the calling account permission before returning restricted function data.
A visible menu, client check or authenticated request does not establish function authorization.
alternative_explanations: The owner permits the lower role to use this function.
The response is a public shell rather than restricted output.
The apparent role came from a client parameter or the wrong session.
stop_conditions: Stop on missing role/policy evidence, approval, privacy boundary or request/time/byte budget.
Do not create users, elevate privileges, change data or follow unrelated endpoints.

worked_example.scenario: Owner reserves a synthetic administration summary for role admin; member B and admin A use isolated sessions.
worked_example.issue_lead: Member B receives restricted summary fields matching A, with both identities independently observed.
worked_example.protected_control: A paired protected summary denies B while A succeeds; preserve it as evidence of the control.
worked_example.limitation: An admin-looking path or identical login page alone cannot prove a role bypass.

cards.title: Session identity and termination continuity
cards.summary: Separate account/session identity from request labels and compare already reviewed termination observations.
prerequisites: Owner documents the intended identity and termination behavior for the selected synthetic account.
Approved owned reads and reviewed before/after records identify the same session without exposing token values.
permitted_actions: Propose only approved identity/control GET reads using the account-specific isolated cookie jar.
Compare reviewed before/after termination records; this card cannot approve logout, credential edits or token replay.
expected_controls: The trusted backend validates session identity; request account labels are not proof of authentication.
A terminated session cannot retrieve protected fields under the owner-declared termination requirement.
alternative_explanations: A cached response appeared without a fresh server request.
An SSO or another independent session authenticated the request.
The collector changed cookie jars or mislabeled the account.
stop_conditions: Stop on token/credential exposure, unclear session provenance, unapproved transitions or budget exhaustion.
Preserve unknowns; do not guess identities from response prose or treat logout UI as backend invalidation.

worked_example.scenario: A synthetic account has reviewed identity before termination and a protected read afterwards in the same session lineage.
worked_example.issue_lead: A fresh reviewed response returns protected fields after observed termination; verify session lineage and owner policy.
worked_example.protected_control: The same session gets a denial after termination while an independently active account succeeds.
worked_example.limitation: A new login, cache hit or missing termination event prevents a session-invalidation conclusion.
